text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak and Libyan Leader Muammar Gaddafi discuss in Tripoli regional and international political developments and bilateral relations. Mubarak asserts his keenness to exchange views with the Libyan leader in order to strengthen relations between the two peoples.
- Head of the Capital Market Authority, Abdel Hamid Ibrahim, says the volume of trade at the Egyptian stock market reached $600 million in seven months.

- Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi says 12 state oil companies made 1.5 billion pounds of profits in the financial year 1995/96, the largest since their establishment and at an increase of 14 percent over profits in the previous year.
- Head of the meteorological authority, Hussein Zuhdi, says rains are forecast to fall on most parts of the country. Floods are also expected.
- The Higher State Security Court sentenced five terrorists, among 32 defendants, to death for launching nine terrorist operations in 1993.
